# Saad Waseem: profile, services and work

Saad Waseem is an independent AI/ML and data engineer in Lahore, Pakistan. He builds production AI agents (LangGraph, MCP, Claude) for tech teams, and websites, business systems and AI automations for small businesses.

- Location: Lahore, Pakistan (UTC+5). Works remotely with teams in the US and EU.
- Email: saad@saad-dev.com
- Book a free 20-minute call: https://cal.id/saad-saad-dev/onboarding-call?duration=20
- Website: https://saad-dev.com
- Profiles: https://github.com/s-wasim, https://linkedin.com/in/s-waseem
- Current role: Lead developer of AI Reports at Maiden Century (Claude agents over 100GB+ of financial data, three report tiers in production)
- Rate for engineering work: $40/hr for build work
- Knows: AI agents, LangGraph, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Anthropic Claude, Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), Human-in-the-loop automation, Data engineering, Apache Airflow, Snowflake, Databricks, Python, Web development

## About (from the CV)

AI/ML and data engineer in Lahore, working remotely with US and EU teams. Lead developer of AI Reports at Maiden Century — Claude agents over 100GB+ of financial data, three tiers in production. Four years of pipelines that run without me watching them.

AI Reports · agents over 100GB+ of financial data: Claude agents through the Anthropic SDK and LangGraph, reading a row-level-secured MCP server so an analyst can only ever see their own entitlements. Three tiers shipped and in production: Ticker Summary, Company Report, Metric Findings.

A: An independent AI/ML and data engineer in Lahore, Pakistan, working remotely with US and EU teams. Lead developer of AI Reports at Maiden Century: Claude agents over 100GB+ of financial data, three report tiers in production.

Q: Can I hire him to build an AI agent for my team?

Q: How does he keep agents safe in production?
A: The graph is drawn before any prompt is written. Data access goes through a row-level-secured MCP server, every agent has a budget of model calls, checks that don't need a model are plain code, and anything a person should sign off on waits at an approval gate.

Q: Does he work with small businesses too?
A: Yes: websites, business systems, AI assistants and automations, at fixed prices from $200 after a free 20-minute audit. See saad-dev.com/services.

## Services for small businesses

How every job works: Free 20-minute audit: A call about what is slowing the business down, and what I would build to fix it. A fixed quote: One price for the whole job, agreed before any work starts. No hourly meter running. 50% up front, 50% on delivery: Half to start, half on delivery, after a 7-day review against the agreed scope. Two months of support: Fixes and small changes are included for two months (up to 5 hours a month). After that, $30/hr if you need me.
Any software subscriptions are in your name and paid by you directly, so you own everything.

## Public work

### document_pipeline: Document AI · human-in-the-loop

https://saad-dev.com/cv/work/document-pipeline/ (source: https://github.com/s-wasim/document_pipeline)

Claude-vision state machine. Any document in, a validated row out. Three LLM calls, one repair attempt, one human gate, 69 tests.

Upload a PDF or a photo of a document; Claude classifies it, extracts the fields into a schema, a non-AI check validates the numbers, one repair attempt runs if they do not add up, and a person approves before anything is written to the database.

- LangGraph pipeline: load → classify → extract → validate → (one repair loop) → review queue.
- Claude's native PDF and vision input, so there is no separate OCR service.
- Cross-field validation is plain code, not an LLM: cheap and deterministic.
- At most three LLM calls per document: classify, extract and an optional repair.
- A review queue shows the document next to the extracted fields; Approve & Commit writes the rows in one transaction.

Stack: Python, LangGraph, Anthropic Claude, Pydantic, PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, Streamlit, Docker
By the numbers: 69 tests, ≤3 LLM calls per document, 1 repair attempt, 1 human approval gate

### Portfolio-Summarizer: Data platform · MCP · agent

https://saad-dev.com/cv/work/portfolio-summarizer/ (source: https://github.com/s-wasim/Portfolio-Summarizer)

Three sources, fourteen tables, three tiers — raw Parquet, a DuckDB warehouse, and derived scores in their own partition. Loads are idempotent: append dedupes on a declared primary key, so a re-run costs nothing. The agent is the last mile, not the point.

An Airflow-orchestrated data platform that pulls SEC filings, prices and news every day, lands them in a 14-table DuckDB warehouse, scores each ticker from −100 to +100, and lets a Claude agent query it all through an MCP server.

- Daily Airflow DAGs extract from SEC EDGAR, Yahoo Finance and Alpha Vantage.
- Three tiers: raw Parquet, a 14-table DuckDB warehouse, and derived scores in their own partition.
- Idempotent loads: appends dedupe on a declared primary key, so a re-run costs nothing.
- A five-module scoring model: price signals, EPS prediction, financial health and qualitative signals, then a final module that blends them into one score.
- An MCP server exposes named DuckDB queries as tools; a Claude agent (LangGraph) answers questions about the portfolio.

Stack: Apache Airflow, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, MCP, LangGraph, Anthropic Claude, Docker Compose
By the numbers: 3 data sources, 14 tables, 5 scoring modules, score from −100 to +100

### inbound_lead_responder: Email agent · human handover

https://saad-dev.com/cv/work/inbound-lead-responder/ (source: https://github.com/s-wasim/inbound_lead_responder)

Six-node email agent. Classifies, extracts, routes on a rules table, drafts a proposal — then hands it to the right team. Nothing goes back to the lead without a person.

An email agent that reads inbound messages, sorts real leads from spam and support, extracts the lead's details, routes it to the right team using an editable rules table, and drafts a proposal document — then hands it to that team in an internal email, so a person decides what goes back to the lead.

- A six-node LangGraph graph: it classifies the email, extracts the lead, routes it, drafts the proposal and hands it over.
- Routing follows a keyword rules table the team can edit; Claude only breaks ties.
- Proposals are generated as Word documents with python-docx.
- At most four Claude calls per lead email.
- Every run has a node-by-node trace, so you can see why a lead went where it did.

Stack: Python, LangGraph, Anthropic Claude, PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, python-docx, Streamlit, Docker
By the numbers: 6 nodes, ≤4 Claude calls per lead, 0 emails sent to the lead automatically

### FaceClusterer: Computer vision · clustering

https://saad-dev.com/cv/work/face-clusterer/ (source: https://github.com/s-wasim/FaceClusterer)

SigLIP global embeddings and InsightFace face embeddings, voted into a consensus across six thresholds. No model retraining, no labels.

Point it at a folder of photos and it groups them by who is in them: SigLIP image embeddings and InsightFace face embeddings are clustered by a consensus vote across six thresholds, giving stable identity labels with no retraining, no labels and no fixed number of clusters.

- Global image embeddings from SigLIP (google/siglip-so400m-patch14-384), batched and GPU-accelerated when available.
- Face detection and face embeddings from InsightFace (buffalo_l).
- Ensemble and consensus clustering across six thresholds, so identities stay stable on noisy photo sets.
- Results are written into browsable folders and zipped.

Stack: Python, SigLIP, InsightFace, NumPy
By the numbers: 6 thresholds, 0 labels needed, 0 retraining

### self_spawnAgents: Multi-agent system · guardrails

https://saad-dev.com/cv/work/self-spawn-agents/ (source: https://github.com/s-wasim/self_spawnAgents)

Four agents, no human in the revenue loop — and a profit-blind ethics auditor that can veto the other three. Frozen-config hashes, a sandboxed code generator, capped budgets per child. 140 tests.

A reference implementation of a four-agent system: a controller that proposes new ventures, a sandboxed code builder, capped-budget child agents, and a profit-blind ethics auditor that can veto the other three.

- Mother agent: a stateful LangGraph controller that manages cash flow across three pots.
- Code builder: stateless, generating tools inside a gVisor sandbox.
- Ethics auditor: profit-blind, with a frozen prompt, and the power to veto.
- Child agents: one per venture, each with a capped budget.
- Frozen-config integrity: changing a protected file trips an alarm unless its hash is re-signed; an operator kill switch works over email.

Stack: Python, LangGraph, Anthropic Claude, PostgreSQL, Docker, gVisor
By the numbers: 4 agents, 140 tests, frozen-config hashes, capped budgets per child

### ai_knowledge_bot: RAG · cited answers

https://saad-dev.com/cv/work/ai-knowledge-bot/ (source: https://github.com/s-wasim/ai_knowledge_bot)

Point it at a codebase, ask it how onboarding works. Every answer carries file:line citations, so a wrong answer is falsifiable in one click.

A retrieval-augmented (RAG) app for getting up to speed on an unfamiliar codebase: ingest a repository, ask questions in plain English, and get answers grounded in the code with clickable file:line citations. When the code does not answer the question, it says so instead of guessing.

- Ingests a local folder or a public GitHub repo, chunked with a line-window chunker.
- Two retrieval modes: Postgres full-text search, or voyage-code-3 embeddings with pgvector.
- A LangGraph flow rewrites the question, grades the retrieved chunks, then answers with citations.
- At most three Claude calls per question.
- An explicit 'not found' path, and every retrieved chunk and grade visible in the UI.

Stack: Python, LangGraph, Anthropic Claude, Voyage AI, PostgreSQL, pgvector, Streamlit, Docker
By the numbers: ≤3 Claude calls per question, file:line citations, 2 retrieval modes
